nodes.content: Design distributed garbage collection that safely reclaims cycles despite concurrent object migration, network partitions, and crash recovery.
requirements: Never reclaim objects reachable through durable roots or in-flight references during crashes, partitions, and migration.
Reclaim unreachable cycles within 3 collection rounds after recovery and quiescence, without global pauses.

nodes.content: Use durable reference/message logs, atomic migration handoffs, and concurrent epoch tracing; sweep unmarked cycles after two fully acknowledged rounds.
How can an epoch close without overlooking references in unacknowledged messages or migration handoffs across a partition?
Epoch closure waits for durable message and migration acknowledgments, preventing partition-time false reclamation and clearing quiescent cycles within three rounds.
Model-check CrashPartition-500 migration, delayed-acknowledgment, and crash-recovery schedules for reference safety and three-round cycle reclamation after quiescence.
CrashPartition-500 found receiver crashes before persisting migration acknowledgment; replay omits acknowledgment, retaining an unreachable cycle past three quiescent rounds.
Persist receipts and migration acceptance before exposure; replay lost acknowledgments from receiver WALs to reclaim quiescent cycles within three rounds.
Rerun CrashPartition-500 comparing volatile versus WAL-persisted acknowledgments; check epoch closure, reachable-object safety, and post-quiescence reclamation rounds.
CrashPartition-500: acknowledgment gating caused zero reachable-object deletions; WAL replay retained duplicate handoff records, delaying cycle reclamation to round four.
Keep acknowledgment gates for safety; persist receiver receipts and deduplicate handoff IDs to eliminate crash-lost acknowledgments and fourth-round delays.
Use durable reference escrows and atomic migration handoffs; partition-fenced trial deletion reclaims isolated cycles within three quiescent rounds.
How can trial deletion distinguish escrowed in-flight references from internal cycle edges when migration overlaps a partition?
Generation-tagged durable escrows distinguish internal cycle edges; unresolved external references block deletion until reconciliation, then reclaim within three rounds.
Run EscrowPartition-1K with partitioned handoffs and generation rollover; measure reachable deletions and quiescent cycle reclamation rounds.
EscrowPartition-1K showed zero reachable deletions across 1,000 schedules; all isolated cycles reclaimed by quiescent round three.
Extend EscrowPartition-1K with receiver crashes and duplicated generation-tagged escrows; verify external-edge classification and post-recovery round-three reclamation.
EscrowPartition-1K crash extension: duplicate generation-tagged escrows appeared external, leaving 37 unreachable cycles unreclaimed after recovery round three.
Durable transfer-ID deduplication removes phantom external escrows while unacknowledged handoffs remain protected, restoring three-round post-recovery reclamation.
Compare generation-only and durable transfer-ID deduplication on EscrowPartition-1K crash schedules; count false external escrows, reachable deletions, and reclamation rounds.
Transfer-ID deduplication eliminated 37 phantom escrows, caused zero reachable deletions, and reclaimed every unreachable cycle by post-recovery round three.
Stress transfer-ID deduplication under WAL compaction, delayed partition-heal messages, and migration; verify escrow classification, reachable-object safety, and reclamation rounds.
After WAL compaction, delayed partition-heal messages recreated 12 phantom escrows from forgotten transfer IDs; 12 cycles survived round three.
Persist per-sender contiguous accepted-transfer watermarks and sparse IDs across compaction; deduplicate delayed replays, preserving live escrows and three-round reclamation.
Replay EscrowPartition-1K with compaction and out-of-order partition-heal messages; check watermark classification, reachable deletions, and post-recovery reclamation rounds.
EscrowPartition-1K found three reachable deletions: restarted senders reused sequence numbers below persisted watermarks, suppressing fresh escrows.
Compare watermark-only and incarnation-qualified escrows under sender-restart sequence collisions in EscrowPartition-1K; measure reachable deletions and reclamation rounds.
Watermark-only prevented phantom escrows and achieved round-three reclamation in 997 noncolliding schedules; incarnation qualification prevented three restart-collision deletions.
Persist sender incarnations before transfers; incarnation-keyed watermarks reject old replays without suppressing fresh escrows, enabling three-round reclamation.
Model-check EscrowPartition-1K with incarnation-persistence crashes, compaction, partition-heal replays, and concurrent migration; measure reachable deletions and reclamation rounds.
EscrowPartition-1K found zero reachable deletions or phantom escrows; all unreachable cycles cleared by round three after recovery and quiescence.
Adopt persisted sender incarnations with compaction-safe per-incarnation watermarks, eliminating restart collisions while retaining round-three reclamation.
Use barrier-protected distributed snapshots capturing channels and migration forwarding; asynchronously trace durable roots and sweep confirmed unmarked cycles.
How can snapshots retire stale migration forwarding entries after crash recovery without hiding live references or delaying cycle reclamation?
Retire forwarding entries after durable destination receipts and channel-drain certificates; preserve unresolved handoffs and reclaim cycles within three rounds.
Model-check SnapshotHandoff-2K with partitioned channels, destination crashes, and forwarding retirement; count reachable deletions and quiescent reclamation rounds.
SnapshotHandoff-2K showed zero reachable deletions across 2,000 schedules; all unreachable cycles reclaimed within three post-quiescence rounds.
Extend SnapshotHandoff-2K with certificate-log compaction and delayed channel replays; test forwarding retirement safety and three-round reclamation.
Compaction erased channel-drain sequence bounds; delayed reference replays bypassed retired forwarding entries, causing two reachable deletions.
Persist channel-drain bounds and nonroot migration redirects through compaction; route delayed references safely while reclaiming cycles within three rounds.
Rerun SnapshotHandoff-2K compaction/replay schedules comparing ephemeral and persisted channel bounds plus redirects; measure reachable deletions and reclamation rounds.
Persisted bounds restored zero reachable deletions, supporting certified retirement; redirects created 19 phantom external edges, delaying reclamation past round three.
Adopt durable channel-drain bounds and routing-only redirects; erased bounds caused deletions, while traced redirects delayed reclamation.
Implement acknowledgment-gated receipts, deduplicated handoffs, incarnation-keyed escrows, and durable channel bounds; validate routing-only redirects and three-round reclamation.
Implement WAL-backed acknowledgment gates, incarnation-keyed escrow deduplication, durable channel bounds, and routing-only redirects in collector prototype v0.1.
Collector prototype v0.1 implements WAL-backed acknowledgment gates, incarnation-keyed escrows, durable drain bounds, and routing-only migration redirects.
